+---
+name: fork-sync
+description: Keep a fork of NeoTech/Camcraft in step with upstream - sync the fork's `main` to the newest cut tag (never to `upstream/main`), and pull the process files (AGENTS.md, skills, agents, xtask, gate wrappers) at the start of each session when upstream's `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is higher. Use at the start of each session in a repository that has an `upstream` remote, before you claim work, and when a PR from a fork conflicts with upstream's main.
+---
+
+# fork-sync - a fork follows cut tags; its rules follow upstream
+
+The rule is in AGENTS.md: "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag, not
+continuously". If this skill and AGENTS.md disagree, AGENTS.md is correct.
+
+## 1. Is this a fork?
+
+`git remote get-url upstream`. A fork of NeoTech/Camcraft has this remote.
+The canonical repository does not: there, use AGENTS.md "Start from the
+latest main" and stop here.
+
+## 2. Process files, at the start of each session
+
+Process files do not change product code. Thus the fork's code stays on the
+tag while its rules stay current. This is the one exception to "sync only to
+a cut tag".
+
+1. `git fetch upstream --tags`.
+2. Compare `git show upstream/main:.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with the local
+   `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.
+3. If upstream's number is higher, pull only the process files:
+
+   ```
+   git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills \
+     .claude/PROCESS_VERSION xtask .cargo/config.toml scripts/gate.ps1 \
+     scripts/gate.sh scripts/release.ps1 scripts/collect-decisions.ps1 \
+     scripts/collect-decisions.sh crates/ui/AGENTS.md
+   ```
+
+4. Commit on a `process-sync` branch: `chore(process): sync process files
+   to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>`.
+5. Merge the branch into the fork's `main`. If the fork protects `main`,
+   open a PR there.
+6. Read AGENTS.md again before you continue.
+
+If the fork's cut tag is older than `xtask/` (the first cut after #748), add
+`"xtask"` to the `members` of the root `Cargo.toml` in the same commit, and
+let `Cargo.lock` take the new package. The wrappers call `cargo xtask`, which
+needs the member. It adds no product code.
+
+The number moves a short time after the files. A fork that synced between
+the two pulls the same files again at the bump. That does no harm.
+
+The pinned issue #681 ("Process changes") says what changed and why. A fork
+maintainer subscribes to it.
+
+## 3. Code, at each cut tag
+
+1. Find the newest cut tag:
+   `git tag -l 'v*.*.0' --sort=-v:refname | head -1`.
+2. Check if the fork's `main` contains it:
+   `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tag> main`.
+3. If it does not: `git switch main && git merge --ff-only <tag>`. Use `git
+   merge <tag>` if the fork's `main` has its own commits. Then `git push
+   origin main`.
+4. Sync only to a cut tag, never to `upstream/main`. A tag is the tested,
+   released state. Upstream's `main` moves many times each hour.
+
+## 4. Issue work in a fork
+
+- Branch issue work from the fork's synced `main` (AGENTS.md "Start from
+  the latest main").
+- A PR into upstream targets upstream's `main`.
+- If the PR conflicts there, merge the upstream change into that branch
+  only (`git merge upstream/main`). Never merge it into the fork's `main`.
+  AGENTS.md "Refresh only at merge time" says when.
+- Write the tag in the PR body: "fork synced at vX.Y.0".

@@ -0,0 +1,152 @@
+---
+name: gate
+description: Run and select the CamCraft test gates with `cargo xtask gate` - the quick, batch and release tiers, one test by name, `--only` / `--failed` / `--dry-run`, the heavy lanes, the slow binaries, the narrow gate ladder for a subagent, the shared sccache compile cache, the pixel-snapshot lane and the local batch gate when the post-merge runner is down. Use before you run tests for a patch, a merge batch or a cut, when a gate step is red and you want to run only that step, or when a worktree builds slowly.
+---
+
+# gate - run the correct tests, and no more
+
+The rules are in AGENTS.md: "Three gate tiers", "Test the change, not
+everything", "Pixel snapshots are release-lane", "Fixes are tested in the
+background". This skill has the mechanics. If the two disagree, AGENTS.md is
+correct.
+
+## The command
+
+`cargo xtask gate <tier>` runs on Windows, macOS and Linux (#748). The
+wrappers `scripts/gate.ps1` (`-Tier quick`, `-Test <name>`) and
+`scripts/gate.sh` (`quick`, `test <name>`) forward to it. Logs go to
+`gate-logs/<tier>-<timestamp>/`.
+
+| Tier | Command | Runs |
+|---|---|---|
+| quick | `cargo xtask gate quick [--base main]` | Only the test binaries that the diff touches, from the gate maps and the touched crates. Debug. No heavy lanes. Target: 5 minutes. |
+| batch | `cargo xtask gate batch` | Each debug suite that is not in `SLOW_BINARIES`, the `camcraft-kernel` suites (#1702), the ui suites from `crates/ui`, clippy. No release-mode heavy lanes. Target: 20 minutes. |
+| release | `cargo xtask gate release` | All debug suites and the `--ignored` heavy lanes in release. Only at a cut. On the cut runner: `cargo xtask gate release --no-snapshots`. |
+| test | `cargo xtask gate test <name> [--crate c] [--binary b] [--exact]` | One test by name. The plain form is `cargo test -p <crate> --test <binary> -- <name> --exact`. |
+
+Flags:
+
+- `--dry-run` (each tier): print the plan and run nothing.
+- `--only <step>` (each tier but `test`, repeatable): run only the named
+  steps. Give the step name or its first word, for example `kernel`,
+  `clippy`, `ui`.
+- `--failed gate-logs/<run>` (each tier but `test`): run only the steps
+  that failed in that run (#1702).
+- `--dry-run` with `--only` or `--failed` shows the selected steps.
+
+A fix for one red step then costs one step, not a full run.
+
+## What quick selects
+
+Quick prints its selection before it runs:
+
+- The changed `#[test]` functions of a changed suite (`--exact`).
+- The gate-mapped suites of a changed source module. The header of each
+  suite has the map: `Gate map (M4.4): covers app::x, app::y...`.
+- A change to shared test code (`tests/common`, goldens, snapshots) runs the
+  suites of that crate.
+- A change in geometry, cl or a `Cargo.toml` falls back to batch.
+- A change in `xtask/` runs the unit tests of xtask.
+- `camcraft-kernel` runs in quick only when kernel is touched.
+
+## Slow binaries and heavy lanes
+
+- Batch does not run the debug binaries in `SLOW_BINARIES`
+  (`xtask/src/plan.rs`, pinned by its unit tests): motion `finish3d`,
+  `pivot5d`, `flow`; app `center_cut_multiaxis`. Each takes 40-50 s. Release
+  runs them.
+- A test that takes more than about 60 s in debug moves to the heavy lane,
+  or gets a smaller fixture. The ignore reason names the lane.
+- Heavy lane tests are `#[ignore]`d. They measure geometry (envelope scans,
+  full-precision projections) or generate over the large fixtures. Run them
+  with `cargo test --release -p camcraft-app -- --ignored`, at a cut and
+  before a push of risky work. Do not run them for each edit.
+- In the release tier, the heavy lanes of motion and app are one release
+  build (`--no-run`). Then there is one step for each test target that can
+  hold an ignored test: `<crate> heavy: lib`, `bins`, `doc` and `<crate>
+  heavy: <binary>` (#1714).
+- One red binary is one red step. Its note names the failed tests and each
+  test that libtest reports as running for more than 60 s.
+- Run one heavy binary again with `--only "app heavy: <binary>"`.
+- When you move a test to a lane, the `#[test]` count before and after must
+  be the same, and the ignored set keeps its golden asserts.
+
+## The narrow ladder (gate subagent)
+
+1. Build one time: `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run`.
+2. Select the binaries from the gate maps, not from the full tree.
+3. Run each test binary that the diff touches
+   (`target\debug\deps\<name>-<hash>.exe`). Run them in parallel: they take
+   no cargo lock. Take the binary paths from the cargo JSON output. Do not
+   glob `*.exe`: that can start the GUI.
+4. Report pass or fail for each binary, with the failure output.
+
+The budget is 5 minutes of wall time. A gate subagent runs this ladder. The
+main session owns the code and the decision to commit. Never give one
+subagent the code change and its verification.
+
+## UI suites and snapshots
+
+- The UI snapshot binaries find their goldens from `crates/ui`. Run them
+  with that working directory. From a different directory they fail with
+  "Missing snapshot".
+- The snapshot lane is in the release tier only: debug, `--ignored
+  snapshot`, working directory `crates/ui`.
+  - `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- --ignored snapshot`
+  - `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test gpu_render -- --ignored snapshot`
+- Do not use `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1` on a PR or at a merge. The goldens are made
+  new at the cut only (`release-cut` skill).
+- `VisualRunner` is enabled automatically. Windows show, run fast, and stay
+  open if a person closes them early. A hidden run stops after 30 s. The
+  window closes 10 s after the last pending test. After a crash or a timeout
+  the window stays open.
+
+## Shared compile cache (optional, #900)
+
+Each worktree has its own `target/`, thus a new worktree compiles each
+third-party crate again. [sccache](https://github.com/mozilla/sccache) makes
+those compilations cache hits.
+
+- Install: `cargo install sccache --locked` (user account only).
+- `cargo xtask gate` sets `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache` and
+  `SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE=20G` for its cargo calls when `sccache` is on PATH.
+- An existing `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, or `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`, has priority.
+- A machine without sccache builds as before.
+- For plain `cargo`, set `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache` only when `sccache` is on
+  PATH. Cargo fails if the wrapper is missing.
+- Never export `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. sccache hashes the `CARGO_*` variables,
+  thus that variable makes each worktree miss the cache.
+- Release packaging never uses the cache. `cargo xtask release` clears the
+  wrapper for the packaging build.
+- The cache is in the sccache default directory: Windows
+  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Mozilla\sccache\cache`, Linux `~/.cache/sccache`.
+  `SCCACHE_DIR` moves it.
+- Dev builds have line tables only. `--config profile.dev.debug=true` gives
+  the variable debug information back for a debugger.
+
+## Local batch gate when the post-merge runner is down
+
+`post-merge.yml` tests each push to `main` (`runners` skill). Use this
+procedure only when its run is queued with no runner, or when it skipped
+itself for a cut and the cut was abandoned.
+
+1. Run one gate for each merge batch, not one for each merge.
+2. Dispatch a gate-runner subagent. It runs `cargo xtask gate batch` on
+   `origin/main` in the MAIN checkout and uses the `target/` of that
+   checkout. Never use a new worktree for it: its `target/` is about 25 GB.
+3. Do not wait for it. Claim the next issue and work in a worktree.
+4. The gate runs in the main checkout only when all of these are true:
+   - The checkout is on a clean `main` (`git pull --ff-only` first).
+   - No `release/*` branch is checked out and no cut is in progress.
+   - No other gate runs there.
+5. Do not start a cut until a running gate is complete.
+6. Check the free disk space before you dispatch. Run `cargo clean` on the
+   main `target/` only when no gate or cut runs and it is larger than about
+   60 GB.
+7. A red result is a new issue with `source:agent`. It is `P1` if the output
+   is wrong or there is a gouge, else `P2`. The issue names the failed tests
+   and the merge that broke them. A red result does not revert the merge.
+
+To hand-test a build between cuts: run `cargo xtask release --version <next>
+--no-tag --skip-gate` on a scratch branch off main (it refuses `--no-tag` on
+main). Then discard the branch and its version bump. Make no tag and no push.

+---
+name: issue-claims
+description: Decide if a claim on a NeoTech/Camcraft issue is live, stale, withdrawn or released, mirror a contributor's claim comment to the `claimed` label, release an ended claim with the fixed comment texts, run the claim maintenance sweep, and work a `needs-research` umbrella issue into sub-issues. Use before you claim an issue that has claim comments or the `claimed` label, at each issue pick and each `/review-prs` run (maintenance), when a contributor writes `claimed:` or `/claim` or withdraws, and when you research a `needs-research` issue.
+---
+
+# issue-claims - who holds an issue, and when it is free again
+
+The rules are in AGENTS.md: "Claim before any code", "A claim comment is a
+claim", "A claim must be live", "`needs-research` is research, not code".
+This skill has the steps and the fixed texts. If the two disagree, AGENTS.md
+is correct. Load `gh-issues` for the `gh` mechanics.
+
+Two kinds of claim:
+
+| Claimant | Claim | Stale after |
+|---|---|---|
+| An agent of the owner account | `claimed` label, assignee, claim comment | 4 hours with no newer comment from the claimant |
+| A contributor (cannot set labels) | A comment that starts with `claimed:` or `/claim` | 48 hours with none of the three signs below |
+
+Never change the labels of a `P?` issue, stale claim or not. Report it to
+the maintainer.
+
+## 1. Check before you claim
+
+1. `gh issue view N --comments`.
+2. Find the newest claim line and its author.
+3. Read the claimant's LAST comment, not only the claim line.
+4. A live claim by a person who is not the owner account means that the
+   issue is taken. Do not work it, with or without the `claimed` label.
+
+## 2. Is a contributor's claim live?
+
+It is live while one or more of these is true:
+
+- The claimant has an open PR for the issue.
+- The claimant's branch for the issue has a commit in the last 48 hours.
+- The claimant commented on the issue in the last 48 hours. Each comment of
+  the claimant counts: the claim, progress, findings. A research claim has no
+  branch, thus the comment keeps it live.
+
+Ended is stronger than live:
+
+- A comment that withdraws or releases a claim is not activity.
+- An ended claim is never live again.
+- Only a NEW `claimed:` or `/claim` comment after the end is a claim.
+- Never mirror an ended claim from its old comment.
+
+## 3. Mirror a live claim
+
+An issue with a live claim comment and no label:
+
+1. Add `claimed` and the claimant as assignee. If GitHub refuses the
+   assignee, set the label only.
+2. Reply one time: "Claim recorded for @<login> - label and assignee set
+   (only collaborators can set labels; your comment is the claim)."
+
+Only a LIVE earlier claim of a different person holds an issue against a new
+claimant. If a new claimant comes after a stale claim: release the stale
+claim first (step 4), then mirror the new claim. The label and the assignee
+always follow the newest live claim.
+
+## 4. Release a stale claim
+
+With none of the three signs, the claim is stale. Do not mirror it. If the
+issue has `claimed`:
+
+1. Remove the label and the assignment.
+2. Comment: "claim by @<login> released (stale: no open PR, branch commit or
+   comment from the claimant for 48 h) - issue is free again; claim it again
+   with a new comment if you are working on it".
+
+That comment ends the claim. A later comment by the claimant does not start
+it again.
+
+## 5. Withdrawn or released
+
+A claim also ends when:
+
+- Its comment is deleted.
+- The claimant's later comment withdraws it: `unclaim`, `/unclaim`, "claim
+  withdrawn", "releasing this claim", "the issue is free".
+- The maintainer releases it in a comment.
+- An agent released it as stale (step 4).
+
+Then remove `claimed` and the assignment, and comment "claim by @<login>
+withdrawn - issue is free again". The comment is not necessary where a
+release comment already says so.
+
+## 6. Owner-account agent claims
+
+- A `claimed` label from an agent of the owner account follows the 4 hour
+  rule, not the 48 hour rule.
+- If the last claim comment is more than 4 hours old and the claimant made
+  no later comment: comment "reclaimed from <old claimant> (stale)" and take
+  the issue.
+
+## 7. Maintenance sweep
+
+Each `/review-prs` run (its step 4) and each issue pick does this for the
+issues that it touches:
+
+1. Mirror the live claims that are comments only (step 3).
+2. Remove the label where the claim is withdrawn, released or stale (steps
+   4 and 5).
+3. Apply the 4 hour rule to owner-account agent claims (step 6).
+
+## 8. Work a `needs-research` issue
+
+A `needs-research` issue is a large idea with open questions. Pick never
+takes it for code.
+
+1. Claim it as in AGENTS.md "Claim before any code", with `plan: research`.
+   Use no branch, no PR and no lane slot.
+2. Answer the open questions in issue comments: the research and the
+   recorded decisions.
+3. File the sub-issues. Each has one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`,
+   `source:agent` (when an agent files it), a "Done means" line and "Part of
+   #N".
+4. Link the sub-issues from the umbrella issue.
+5. When each sub-issue is filed, remove `needs-research` and close the
+   umbrella with a comment that names them. Do not keep it open: Pick must
+   not take it for code.
+
+Only the sub-issues are picked for code.

+---
+name: release-cut
+description: Cut a CamCraft minor or major release, step by step - the start condition (no open P1/P2), review and merge of the waiting feat PRs, the release branch with decisions, release notes and changelog rows, the release gate on the cut runner (`cut.yml` stage gate), the release PR, the tag (`cut.yml` stage tag), `release.yml`, the `shipped in` comments and the documentation site check. Use when the maintainer asks for a cut, a release, a tag or "ship X.Y.0", or when you must know what a late P1/P2 does to a cut in progress.
+---
+
+# release-cut - PR review, merge to main, tag
+
+The rules are in AGENTS.md "Commits and Releases": "Versioning is semantic",
+"When to cut", "A cut goes PR review -> merge to main -> tag", "Every cut tag
+is published". This skill has the procedure. If the two disagree, AGENTS.md
+is correct.
+
+Cuts and tags stay with the maintainer. Do not start a cut without his
+instruction. Only minor and major versions are cut: there are no patch cuts.
+
+From step 1 to the tag, nothing else merges to `main`.
+
+## Step 1 - Start condition, then review and merge the issue PRs
+
+Start condition (#1424):
+
+1. Check that no `P1` or `P2` issue is open. If one is open, the cut does
+   not start. A `P3` or lower does not hold a cut.
+2. Record the UTC start time and that list (none) in the release PR body.
+3. A `P1` or `P2` issue filed after that moment does not restart the cut and
+   does not enter it. The cut completes on the tree that passed the release
+   gate.
+4. Name each such issue under "Known issues" (step 2 and step 3). Its fix
+   merges after the tag and ships in the next minor.
+5. Only the maintainer can stop a cut for it. No agent stops or restarts a
+   cut for a late issue.
+6. An agent that finds a late `P1` (unsafe or wrong output) tells the
+   maintainer in one line and continues.
+7. A failure of the cut's own release gate is not a late issue. Fix it in
+   the cut.
+
+Review and merge:
+
+1. Each open `in-review` `feat` or breaking PR gets a review by a subagent
+   that did not write it (`/code-review` on the PR, or a reviewer that gets
+   the diff and not the author's conclusion). Fix the findings on that
+   branch and push.
+2. A PR that does not merge cleanly is refreshed at merge time, in the order
+   that `cargo xtask merge-plan` gives (AGENTS.md "Refresh only at merge
+   time"): `git merge origin/main` on its branch, quick gate, push. An old
+   branch that still appends to `RECOMMENDED.md` keeps the two sides.
+3. Stacked PRs: retarget each child to `main` before you merge its parent
+   (AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack"). Then merge the parent first.
+4. Remove a worktree that holds the branch before the merge. The local
+   branch delete fails if you do not.
+5. `gh pr merge M --merge --delete-branch`. Use merge commits, never squash
+   or rebase: the branch commits keep the hashes that the issue comments
+   name.
+
+## Step 2 - Release branch
+
+1. Sync main: `git pull --ff-only`. Then `git switch -c release/vX.Y.Z`.
+   The version is the highest bump of the commits since the last tag
+   (AGENTS.md "Versioning is semantic").
+2. Run `cargo xtask decisions --version X.Y.Z`. It appends each
+   `docs/decisions/*.md` to `RECOMMENDED.md` under a `vX.Y.Z` heading and
+   removes the files.
+3. Write `RELEASE_NOTES.md`.
+   - While the major is 0, a breaking change bumps MINOR. The notes then say
+     "breaking" first.
+   - Add a "Known issues" section: each `P1` or `P2` filed after the start,
+     by number and title.
+   - Add a "Process changes" section: each `PROCESS_VERSION` since the
+     previous tag, from the pinned issue #681.
+4. Write the `CHANGELOG.md` rows for each PR merged since the previous tag:
+   one row for each behaviour PR, from its `Changelog:` line, plus the rows
+   marked `Unreleased`. Fix PRs merge between cuts, thus include them. The
+   row format:
+   `| <short merge commit> | <YYYY-MM-DD> | <change, one line> (#N, PR #M) | X.Y.Z |`.
+5. Commit items 2-4 together: `docs: X.Y.Z release notes; changelog`.
+6. Run `cargo xtask release --version X.Y.Z --no-tag --skip-gate`. It
+   commits the version bump and makes no tag. It refuses `--no-tag` on main.
+   - Its local zip (and, on Windows with `--installer`, the installer) is a
+     hand-test build only. `release.yml` builds the published zip, installer
+     and packages from the tag.
+   - A packaging failure after its phase 4 does not undo the bump commit.
+7. Two checks stay local, on Windows, before the push:
+   - The pixel-snapshot lanes, working directory `crates/ui`:
+     `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- --ignored snapshot` and
+     `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test gpu_render -- --ignored snapshot`.
+     The goldens were made on Windows. Make them new here, in one commit,
+     only after a human looks at the `.diff.png`.
+   - Optional: the Windows arms of the per-OS pinned readings (for example
+     the move counts of issue 1402 in `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs`).
+     The Linux runner checks only the Linux arm.
+   - A cut without a Windows machine skips the two checks and says so in the
+     release PR.
+
+## Step 3 - Release gate on the cut runner, then the release PR
+
+1. `git push -u origin release/vX.Y.Z`.
+2. Start the gate: `gh workflow run cut.yml -f version=X.Y.Z -f stage=gate`
+   (or Actions -> Cut -> Run workflow, `version` X.Y.Z, `stage` gate).
+   - It checks out `release/vX.Y.Z`.
+   - It refuses a branch whose `Cargo.toml` or `RELEASE_NOTES.md` does not
+     name X.Y.Z, or whose tag exists.
+   - It runs `cargo xtask gate release --no-snapshots`.
+   - It uploads `gate-logs/` as an artifact, green or red.
+   - When green, it records the tested commit.
+   - The `dry_run` input prints the plan only. Use it to try a new runner.
+3. Red: nothing is tagged. Fix on the release branch, push, and start the
+   gate again. After a limited fix, `--only` / `--failed` (`gate` skill) run
+   only the red steps locally before the next full gate.
+4. While the gate runs: `gh pr create --base main --title "chore(release):
+   X.Y.Z"`. It is reviewed as each PR is.
+   - The body has the start-condition record (step 1).
+   - A comment names each `P1` / `P2` filed after the start, as "Known
+     issues".
+5. When the gate is green and the PR is reviewed: `gh pr merge --merge
+   --delete-branch`.
+6. Do not push to the branch after the green gate. The tag stage refuses a
+   merge whose tree is not the gated tree.
+
+## Step 4 - Tag the release merge commit, on the cut runner
+
+1. Start Cut again: `gh workflow run cut.yml -f version=X.Y.Z -f stage=tag`.
+2. It takes `tip`, the commit of the newest green gate run for X.Y.Z, and
+   `m`, the head of main. It refuses unless all of these are true:
+   - `m` is the merge of `tip` by the release PR (`m^2 == tip`): nothing
+     else merged since step 1.
+   - `git diff $tip $m` is empty: the gated tree is the tagged tree.
+   - The tag is free.
+3. Then it makes `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "CamCraft X.Y.Z" $m`, pushes it, and
+   starts `release.yml` on the tag (`gh workflow run release.yml --ref
+   vX.Y.Z`). A tag pushed with the workflow token starts no workflow, thus
+   the explicit start. On a tag ref, `release.yml` publishes as on a pushed
+   tag.
+4. `dry_run` does each check and makes no tag.
+5. A refusal means that something got to main during the cut, or that the
+   branch moved after the gate. Start the cut again from step 2 on a new
+   release branch.
+6. Fallback when the runner is down: run the gate locally, then `git tag`
+   and `git push origin vX.Y.Z` by hand. The push starts `release.yml`. The
+   same empty-diff rule applies.
+7. Comment `shipped in vX.Y.Z` on each issue closed since the previous tag:
+   the merged PRs of the cut and the fix PRs merged since. Remove each
+   `in-review` label that is left.
+
+Never move an existing tag and never push it again. Never force-push. A fix
+after a cut merges to `main` and ships in the next minor.
+
+## Step 5 - Check the documentation site (#688)
+
+- The same tag run makes the Zola site in `site/` from the tagged tree and
+  deploys it to GitHub Pages (`release.yml` jobs `site` and `pages`).
+  `pages` waits for `publish`, thus the download links of the site never
+  point at a release that does not exist.
+- The browser build (`wasm`, #1103) is served at `/app/`. A failed wasm
+  build leaves `/app/` as the "not part of this copy" page with a warning.
+  It does not fail the cut.
+- Commit nothing for the site. Add no trigger.
+- The cut is complete when the `pages` job is green and
+  `https://neotech.github.io/Camcraft/` shows "CamCraft X.Y.Z".
+- Run a red `pages` job again (Actions "Re-run failed jobs"). Never repair
+  it by moving the tag.
+- Local preview: `zola build` in `site/` (`site/README.md`).

+---
+name: runners
+description: The self-hosted GitHub Actions runners and workflows of NeoTech/Camcraft - the cut runner (`cut.yml`), the post-merge gate (`post-merge.yml`), the PR test runner (`pr-test.yml`), the billed-minutes budget of `release.yml`, machine requirements, runner labels, registration and the safety rules. Use when you install or change a runner, change a file in `.github/workflows/`, start or read a `pr-test.yml`, `post-merge.yml` or `cut.yml` run, or must decide if a trigger is permitted.
+---
+
+# runners - self-hosted runners and the workflows on them
+
+The rules are in AGENTS.md: "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted", "The cut
+runner", "The post-merge gate", "The PR test runner". This skill has the
+details. If the two disagree, AGENTS.md is correct.
+
+## Triggers and budget
+
+- The budget is 3000 billed minutes each month. Windows counts 2x and macOS
+  10x.
+- Nothing runs on a PR trigger. The quick and batch tiers run locally
+  (`gate` skill) or on a self-hosted runner.
+- The permitted triggers are `workflow_dispatch`, the tag push of
+  `release.yml`, and the push to `main` of `post-merge.yml` (self-hosted
+  jobs only).
+- Never add a `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger without the
+  maintainer's approval.
+- Never add a trigger that a fork PR can start to a workflow with
+  self-hosted jobs. A fork PR must not run code on the maintainer's machine.
+- `release.yml` runs on a cut tag and publishes the artifact.
+  `aur-package.yml` is a job that `release.yml` calls. `ci.yml` and
+  `nightly.yml` are removed.
+- `cut.yml` (#1413) runs the release tier of a cut on the cut runner. It
+  starts `release.yml`; it does not replace it.
+- Billed minutes of one cut: `cut.yml` 0 (self-hosted). `release.yml` about
+  230 by the job times of v0.18.0 (Linux jobs about 50, Windows 10 x2, macOS
+  16 x10). The measured value is still to be recorded from the release run
+  of the first `cut.yml` cut (Actions -> the run -> Usage).
+
+## The cut runner (#1413)
+
+The jobs of `cut.yml` run on `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]`, never on a
+GitHub-hosted runner. The machine needs:
+
+- Linux x86-64, registered to NeoTech/Camcraft at repository level, with
+  the labels `self-hosted`, `Linux`, `X64`. An added name label is
+  permitted. Size: 16 cores and about 64 GB RAM. Fewer cores work, but
+  slower.
+- Disk: 100 GB free or more for the work directory (a clean `target/` with
+  the release heavy lanes is 20-30 GB), plus the sccache cache.
+- On the PATH of the runner service: the Rust toolchain (`~/.cargo/bin`, a
+  stable rustc that builds the workspace), `git`, `gh`.
+- The Linux build packages that the linux job of `release.yml` installs:
+  `pkg-config`, `libwayland-dev`, `libxkbcommon-dev`, `libx11-dev`.
+- For the UI suites, which open windows: `xvfb` (the workflow puts the gate
+  in `xvfb-run -a` when no display is set) and the Mesa software drivers
+  (`mesa-vulkan-drivers`, `libgl1-mesa-dri`).
+- sccache: in the `.env` of the runner, set `RUSTC_WRAPPER` to the sccache
+  binary and `SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE` (for example 40G). Never set
+  `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Each run builds in the `target/` of the workspace,
+  which `actions/checkout` cleans; the compile cache keeps that cheap.
+
+Registration:
+
+1. The maintainer makes a token: Settings -> Actions -> Runners -> New
+   self-hosted runner, Linux x64.
+2. In the runner directory: `./config.sh --unattended --url
+   https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft --token <token> --name <name>
+   --labels <extra labels> --work <work dir>`.
+3. Run it as a service: `./svc.sh install`, or a user systemd unit with
+   linger enabled, so that it continues after logout.
+
+Safety:
+
+- Run the runner as an account without privileges. No sudo without a
+  password. The `docker` group is equal to root.
+- Keep "Require approval for all outside collaborators" on for fork PR
+  workflows (Settings -> Actions -> General).
+- Never approve the workflow run of a fork PR that adds or changes a file
+  in `.github/workflows/`. Such a file can name `self-hosted`.
+
+## The post-merge gate (#1451)
+
+- `post-merge.yml` runs `cargo xtask gate batch` on each push to `main`,
+  and on `workflow_dispatch` (input `ref`). It never runs on a PR trigger.
+- Its jobs use the runner label `camcraft-post-merge` (the Linux runner
+  `uma`). That runner does not have `camcraft-pr-test`, thus a PR test never
+  waits for a gate.
+- A group of merges tests only the newest head (`cancel-in-progress`).
+- It gives way to the cut. It skips itself (green, with a notice) while a
+  `cut.yml` run is queued or in progress, or while an open `release/vX.Y.Z`
+  PR from this repository exists (`.github/scripts/post-merge-skip.sh`).
+- It reports through `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh`. Only its
+  report job has `issues: write`.
+- A red run opens or comments on the one issue `main is red (post-merge
+  gate)`. The issue is `P2`. It is `P1` only when a failed suite is a
+  wrong-output suite: a golden CL/NC suite or a recorded-post-stream suite,
+  named in the anchored `OUTPUT_SUITES` list of the script.
+- The next green run closes the issue. The workflow closes only an issue
+  with `source:agent`.
+- If the runner is down, use the local batch gate (`gate` skill).
+
+## The PR test runner (#1420)
+
+`pr-test.yml` runs the build and tests of a PR review on the maintainer's
+self-hosted runners. It bills no minutes and needs no 10-20 GB worktree on
+the reviewer's machine.
+
+- Trigger: `workflow_dispatch` only. Inputs: the PR number and the head SHA
+  that the reviewer read. The token is read-only. There are no secrets.
+- It checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` and refuses a different head.
+- It refuses a diff (listed with `--no-renames`) that touches: `build.rs`,
+  `.github/`, `scripts/`, a `.cargo/` directory at any depth, a
+  `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`, a toolchain file, `xtask/`.
+- It trial-merges with main, then runs `cargo xtask gate quick --base
+  origin/main` and clippy on the touched crates. The ui suites run in
+  `xvfb-run` with the Mesa software drivers.
+- Only the PR-reviewer agent starts it, after it read the diff.
+- It runs only for a collaborator's PR. The workflow checks the author's
+  push access and refuses other authors. Other PRs build locally. The
+  refusal list does not stop hostile test code: that is the reason for this
+  rule.
+- Start it only when a runner is online and no cut uses the runner. Never
+  send a "read, not built" PR.
+- If there is no runner, or the run is cancelled, times out or does not
+  start, the review builds locally or says "not built". It never says
+  "pass".
+- The job uses the runner label `camcraft-pr-test`. Each self-hosted runner
+  with the label can take it: Linux (`len`) or macOS (`m3`).
+- On macOS the UI suites open real windows, thus that runner needs a
+  logged-in session. The per-OS pinned readings run the arm of that OS.
+- Each PR test runner has its own OS user, HOME, cargo home and sccache
+  directory. It shares none of them with the cut runner.
+- Windows-only readings (`cfg(windows)`, per-OS pinned values) run locally
+  for the touched suites.
